From d049e56b1739101d1c4d81deedb269c52a8dbba0 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Yasuaki Torimaru <yasuakitorimaru@gmail.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Mar 2026 19:06:24 +0900
Subject: [PATCH] wifi: wilc1000: fix u8 overflow in SSID scan buffer size
 calculation

The variable valuesize is declared as u8 but accumulates the total
length of all SSIDs to scan. Each SSID contributes up to 33 bytes
(IEEE80211_MAX_SSID_LEN + 1), and with WILC_MAX_NUM_PROBED_SSID (10)
SSIDs the total can reach 330, which wraps around to 74 when stored
in a u8.

This causes kmalloc to allocate only 75 bytes while the subsequent
memcpy writes up to 331 bytes into the buffer, resulting in a 256-byte
heap buffer overflow.

Widen valuesize from u8 to u32 to accommodate the full range.

Fixes: c5c77ba18ea6 ("staging: wilc1000: Add SDIO/SPI 802.11 driver")
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Signed-off-by: Yasuaki Torimaru <yasuakitorimaru@gmail.com>
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20260324100624.983458-1-yasuakitorimaru@gmail.com
Signed-off-by: Johannes Berg <johannes.berg@intel.com>

diff --git a/drivers/net/wireless/microchip/wilc1000/hif.c b/drivers/net/wireless/microchip/wilc1000/hif.c
index f354b11cb919..944b2a812b63 100644
--- a/drivers/net/wireless/microchip/wilc1000/hif.c
+++ b/drivers/net/wireless/microchip/wilc1000/hif.c
@@ -163,7 +163,7 @@ int wilc_scan(struct wilc_vif *vif, u8 scan_source,
 	u32 index = 0;
 	u32 i, scan_timeout;
 	u8 *buffer;
-	u8 valuesize = 0;
+	u32 valuesize = 0;
 	u8 *search_ssid_vals = NULL;
 	const u8 ch_list_len = request->n_channels;
 	struct host_if_drv *hif_drv = vif->hif_drv;
-- 
2.34.1

The patch modifies a single file to fix an integer overflow issue that leads to a heap buffer overflow.

### Modifications in each file:
- **drivers/net/wireless/microchip/wilc1000/hif.c**: The variable `valuesize` in `wilc_scan()` was changed from `u8` to `u32`. This variable accumulates the total length of all SSIDs to be scanned. Previously, a `u8` could overflow (max 330 bytes from up to 10 SSIDs each up to 33 bytes), causing an incorrect allocation and subsequent heap buffer overflow.

### Relationship:
The change directly addresses the root cause of the buffer overflow: by widening the accumulator to a 32-bit type, the calculation of the required scan buffer size is no longer truncated, ensuring `kmalloc` allocates sufficient memory and preventing the subsequent `memcpy` from writing beyond the allocated space.

You are a programming expert.

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
<text>
u8 valuesize = 0;
...
for (i = 0; i < request->n_ssids; i++)
    valuesize += ((request->ssids[i].ssid_len) + 1);
</text>
Reason:
`valuesize` is declared as `u8`, which can hold at most 255. Each SSID contributes up to 33 bytes (32 bytes SSID + 1 byte length) and up to 10 SSIDs can be requested, resulting in a total of 330 bytes. This causes integer overflow, wrapping the sum to 74. Consequently, `kmalloc(valuesize + 1)` allocates only 75 bytes, while the subsequent `memcpy` writes up to 331 bytes, causing a 256‑byte heap buffer overflow.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
<text>
u32 valuesize = 0;
</text>
Reason:
Changing the type of `valuesize` from `u8` to `u32` removes the overflow, as `u32` can accommodate the maximum possible sum of 330 bytes. The allocated buffer size and subsequent `memcpy` now match correctly, preventing the heap buffer overflow.
